gold_requirements.text: The THEMAS system shall read the initialization file to derive heating and cooling unit definitions.
The THEMAS system shall load thermostat unique identifiers from the initialization file.
The THEMAS system shall read the maximum number of concurrently running heating or cooling units from the initialization file.
The THEMAS system shall read trigger values from the initialization file.
The THEMAS system shall read overtemperature values from the initialization file.
The THEMAS system shall read the valid temperature range from the initialization file.
The THEMAS system shall turn off all heating and cooling units upon initialization.
The THEMAS system shall identify current temperature values as invalid if they are outside the valid temperature range.
The THEMAS system shall identify temperature settings as invalid if they are outside the valid temperature range.
The THEMAS system shall compare reported temperature values to the temperature setting to detect if limits are exceeded.
The THEMAS system shall activate the appropriate heating or cooling unit when the current temperature exceeds the temperature setting by a predefined amount.
The THEMAS system shall maintain the ON/OFF status of each heating and cooling unit.
The THEMAS system shall add heating or cooling requests to a LIFO queue if the maximum number of units is already running.
The THEMAS system shall record a system event when a heating or cooling request is denied.
The THEMAS system shall generate a control signal for heating or cooling units.
The THEMAS system shall output a continuous series of alternating 500 Hz and 700 Hz beeps when an invalid temperature is detected.
The THEMAS system shall output a continuous series of alternating 1000 Hz and 1500 Hz beeps when a temperature limit is exceeded.
The THEMAS system shall record event data including description and current system time in a database.
The THEMAS system shall provide a mechanism for the supervisor to change the temperature setting of any thermostat.
The THEMAS system shall generate operational history reports and statistical summary reports.
The THEMAS system shall be designed to run on the Microsoft Windows NT operating system.
The THEMAS system shall ensure the temperature reported by a thermostat does not exceed a maximum deviation value of 3 degrees Fahrenheit.
The thermostats shall only provide temperature values and temperature settings.
No signal shall be available to allow the THEMAS system to determine if a signal sent to a heating or cooling unit was realized.
After start-up, the system shall check every thermostat and turn on any unit that's needed.
When the room temperature is within range, the system shall turn the heating and cooling off.
The system shall not let more than the set maximum number of units run at once.
When a unit turns off, the system shall pick the latest waiting request and turn that unit on if it's still needed.
An alarm shall keep beeping until the supervisor switches it off.
